_about: How every SDK (pkg/wakeshift, sdk/typescript, sdk/python) answers MCP Events requests where the three used to differ (items 3 and 4). Each SDK runs every case. SEP-3415 as accepted (revision), over Streamable HTTP on protocol 2026-07-28 (SEP-2243's headers).

mcp_name_decode._comment: Decoding an Mcp-Name header: plain ASCII as it is, or SEP-2243's sentinel =?base64?…?= holding canonical, padded standard Base64 (RFC 4648 §4) of UTF-8, as the 2026-07-28 transport spec's examples and the official SDKs have it. value null: the header is malformed (unpadded, non-canonical, not Base64, not UTF-8), which is a HeaderMismatch whatever params.name is.

mcp_name._comment: Item 3. The app defines chat.message ({channel}) with public: true, and identify gives user u1. Each request is POSTed on protocol 2026-07-28 (MCP-Protocol-Version and Mcp-Method headers) with params {name: chat.message, arguments: {channel: eng}} (events/subscribe adds a webhook delivery; events/list sends no name), _meta naming the client (clientInfo client) and its capabilities, which declare the events extension when declares is true. header: the Mcp-Name header sent (null: none); second_header, when present, a second Mcp-Name field sent after it (more than one is refused, whatever they say). A missing Mcp-Name is accepted from every client, declaring or not (a known deviation from SEP-3415: ChatGPT, OpenClaw, the Vercel AI SDK, Hermes and Mastra don't send it yet). A header that's there must match params.name, from any client, whatever it claims to be. want refused: HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error -32020 (HeaderMismatch), and Wakeshift isn't asked; want passed: anything but that.

mcp_param_schema._comment: SEP-3415's custom headers from subscription arguments, which take the 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP transport's x-mcp-header rules for tools (its Schema Extension). An annotation is valid when it's a non-empty RFC 9110 token (1*tchar), on a property whose type is "string", "integer" or "boolean" (one type: never number, a list or none), reached from the root through properties keys only (never the root itself, items, anyOf, oneOf, allOf, not, if/then/else, additionalProperties, patternProperties, $defs or $ref), and no other annotation in the schema has the same name in any case. A spec client drops an event type with an invalid one from events/list, so defining such an event is a config error in every SDK. schema: the arguments' JSON Schema; valid: whether it's accepted.

mcp_param._comment: The Mcp-Param-{Name} check on events/poll, events/stream, events/subscribe (each refresh) and events/unsubscribe over HTTP, for the event's arguments' schema (schema). Strict, as the spec requires, unlike a missing Mcp-Name: a request whose params.arguments has a value other than null at an annotated property's path (its chain of properties keys) must carry that Mcp-Param-{Name} header (the name in any case), once; a header for an absent or null value, or for a value with no header form (an object, an array), is refused too. The header decodes as Mcp-Name does (mcp_name_decode); a plain value is visible ASCII, spaces and tabs, trimmed at either end of spaces and tabs. The decoded value must equal the body's: a string as it is, a boolean as true or false, an integer (an annotated integer property's whole number) as a number when the header is a plain decimal (42.0 and 042 are 42; no sign, no exponent), else as its decimal text. Headers no annotation names are ignored. arguments: params.arguments; headers: the [name, value] fields sent; want: refused (HeaderMismatch) or passed.

mcp_param_http._comment: mcp_param end to end. The app also defines deploy.finished (public), whose arguments are region (a required string, annotated Region) and attempt (an optional integer, annotated Attempt), and whose payload has both, so events/list gives its inputSchema as input_schema, annotations kept. Each request is POSTed as mcp_name's are (protocol 2026-07-28, Mcp-Method, client tanstack-ai declaring the extension) with params {name: event (absent: deploy.finished), arguments} (events/subscribe adds a webhook delivery), Mcp-Name naming the event unless no_name, and these headers. want refused: HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error -32020 (HeaderMismatch), checked before anything else that could refuse it (events/stream's push refusal included), and Wakeshift isn't asked; passed: anything but that.

stream._comment: Item 4. Where events/stream (push) isn't served (the core doesn't report the push feature, the transport answers with JSON, or the app turned push off; mcp-events-wire.json push has where it is), for any event, known or not: Unsupported, its data naming the delivery mode push (SEP-3415's own example), in the client's dialect (ChatGPT has no Unsupported code: InvalidParams). The Mcp-Name check comes first (mcp_name). Wakeshift isn't asked.

error.message: push delivery isn't offered: use a webhook (events/subscribe) or poll (events/poll)

transport_headers._comment: The 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP transport's standard headers on events/* (its Server Validation, which SEP-3415's Routing Headers apply to events methods), checked by every SDK before anything else on these methods (Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param, the event, push), whatever the MCP SDK under it checks. A request is 2026-07-28 when its MCP-Protocol-Version header or its _meta io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion (meta_version, null: none) names 2026-07-28. Such a request needs MCP-Protocol-Version, equal to _meta's when _meta names one, and Mcp-Method; an Mcp-Method that's sent must equal the body's method exactly, on any request. A legacy request (an initialize session's, legacy: true) may leave Mcp-Method out. Each request is POSTed with params {name: chat.message, arguments: {channel: eng}} (events/list: none; events/subscribe adds a webhook delivery), _meta naming client tanstack-ai and declaring the extension, Mcp-Name chat.message on the named methods, and these headers. want refused: HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error -32020 (HeaderMismatch), and Wakeshift isn't asked; passed: anything but that. An SDK whose host serves no legacy request without a session skips the legacy cases there.

no_events._comment: Item 4. A server attached with no event defined advertises no events capability and answers every events/* method on protocol 2026-07-28 as one it doesn't have: JSON-RPC -32601 (method not found), as SEP-3415 says of a server that doesn't offer the extension (the MCP SDK answers it, with its own HTTP status).

native_client._comment: Item 4, and the client table (mcp-events-clients.json). Whether a request comes from a client that subscribes with MCP Events itself (so tools/list leaves out subscribe_events, events/list lists tools-only events for vouchers, and call.subscribe leaves the subscribing to it), and its dialect: one rule in every SDK and the core, on every path, before the app's own isNativeClient. The table's first matching entry, in file order, decides (never ChatGPT's desktop app; ChatGPT and OpenClaw without declaring; never a harness Wakeshift wakes itself, by client name or User-Agent product, whatever it declares; opencode only while push isn't served); with none, a client is native when it declares the extension, in the request's _meta capabilities or its session's initialize capabilities, in the spec dialect. client: the clientInfo name (the request's _meta, else the session's); user_agent: the HTTP User-Agent; session_extensions: the extensions its session's initialize declared (null: no session); serves_push: whether the server serves push (absent: false). Expected: native, dialect, and entry (the matched entry's id, "" when none matched).
